title: Fraud, The Perils of Clickstream, and International Concerns

cues.en: Another real-world problem is people trying to game your system.
cues.zh: 另一個實務問題，是有人試圖操弄系統。

cues.en: If items your recommender system promotes to your users leads to those items being purchased more, the makers of those items have a financial incentive to find ways to game your system
cues.zh: 如果推薦系統向使用者推廣的項目，確實因此賣得更多，這些項目的製造商，就有金錢上的誘因，設法操弄系統，

cues.en: into recommending their items more often.
cues.zh: 讓它更常推薦自家項目。

cues.en: Or, people with certain ideological agendas might purposely try to make your system recommend items that promote their own ideology, or to not recommend items that run counter to it.
cues.zh: 或者，有特定意識形態目的的人，可能刻意讓系統推薦宣揚其理念的項目，或不要推薦與其理念相反的項目。

cues.en: Some hacker might even be bored, and try to create humorous pairings in your recommender system just for their own amusement.
cues.zh: 甚至可能有駭客只是無聊，為了自娛，在推薦系統裡製造搞笑的配對。

cues.en: Google bombs are an example of this.
cues.zh: Google 炸彈就是例子。

cues.en: Fighting people like this is generally a never-ending arms race, but there is one technique that works remarkably well, make sure that recommendations are only generated from people who actually spent money on the item.
cues.zh: 與這些人對抗，通常是永無止境的軍備競賽，但有個效果非常好的方法：確保推薦只根據真正花錢購買該項目的人產生。

cues.en: Recommendations based on implicit ratings from purchasing data are almost impervious to these sorts of attacks, because it would be prohibitively expensive for someone to buy enough of an item
cues.zh: 根據購買資料的隱含評分做推薦，幾乎不受這類攻擊影響，因為要購買足夠數量的某項商品，

cues.en: to artificially inflate its presence in your recommendations.
cues.zh: 來人為提高它在推薦中的曝光，成本會高得令人卻步。

cues.en: And, when people vote with their wallets, it's a very strong and reliable indication of interest that leads to better recommendations overall.
cues.zh: 而且，人們用錢包投票時，是非常強烈、可靠的興趣訊號，整體上能帶來更好的推薦。

cues.en: Sometimes, however, you don't have enough purchase data to work with.
cues.zh: 不過，有時你沒有足夠的購買資料可用。

cues.en: There are still precautions you can take, however.
cues.zh: 但仍然可以採取一些預防措施。

cues.en: For example, if your recommender system is based on star reviews, you can make sure that you only allow reviews from people you know actually purchased or consumed the content in question.
cues.zh: 例如，若推薦系統根據星等評論，就能確保只允許已確認真正購買或使用過該內容的人評分。

cues.en: If you allow people to rate items they haven't actually seen or used, you're opening yourself up to all sorts of attacks.
cues.zh: 若允許人們為沒有真正看過或用過的項目評分，就是讓自己暴露在各種攻擊之下。

cues.en: And using click data should always be a last resort, it's very easy to fake click data using bots, and even if it's not a bot, click data has its own set of problems.
cues.zh: 使用點擊資料永遠應該是最後手段。機器人很容易偽造點擊資料，而且就算不是機器人，點擊資料本身也有問題。

cues.en: Using implicit clickstream data, such as images people click on, is fraught with problems.
cues.zh: 使用隱含點擊流資料，例如人們點擊的圖片，充滿問題。

cues.en: You should always be extremely skeptical about building a recommender system that relies only on things people click on, such as ads.
cues.zh: 對於只依賴人們點擊內容，例如廣告，來建立推薦系統這件事，你始終應該極度懷疑。

cues.en: Not only are these sorts of systems highly susceptible to gaming, they're susceptible to quirks of human behavior that aren't useful for recommendations.
cues.zh: 這類系統不只非常容易被操弄，也容易受人類行為怪癖影響，而那些怪癖對推薦沒有幫助。

cues.en: I've learned this the hard way a couple of times.
cues.zh: 我曾幾次付出代價，才學到這點。

cues.en: If you ever build a system that recommends products based on product images that people click on when they see them in an online ad, I promise you that what you build will end up as a -- detection system.
cues.zh: 如果建立一個系統，根據人們在網路廣告上看到並點擊的產品圖片來推薦產品，我保證，最後會變成某種偵測系統；原字幕在此省略了被偵測的詞。

cues.en: The reality is, people instinctively click on images that contain images that appear sexual in nature.
cues.zh: 現實是，人們會本能地點擊帶有性暗示的圖片。

cues.en: Your recommender system will end up converging on products that feature pictures that include a lot of flesh, and there won't be anything you can do about it.
cues.zh: 推薦系統最後會收斂到產品照片中露出大量肌膚的商品，而且你無能為力。

cues.en: Even if you explicitly filter out items that are sexual in nature, you'll end up discovering products that just vaguely look like sex toys or various pieces of sexual anatomy.
cues.zh: 即使明確濾除性相關項目，最後也會找到一些只是隱約看起來像情趣用品，或各種性器官的產品。

cues.en: I'm not making this up, I'm probably not at liberty to talk about the details, but I've seen this happen more than once.
cues.zh: 我沒有亂說。大概不方便談細節，但我不只看過一次這種情況。

cues.en: Never, ever build a recommender system based on image clicks!
cues.zh: 千萬不要根據圖片點擊建立推薦系統！

cues.en: And implicit data in general tends to be very low quality, unless it's backed by a purchase or actual consumption.
cues.zh: 一般來說，除非有購買或實際使用行為支持，否則隱含資料的品質往往很差。

cues.en: Clickstream data is a very unreliable signal of interest.
cues.zh: 點擊流資料是非常不可靠的興趣訊號。

cues.en: What people click on and what they buy can be very different things.
cues.zh: 人們點擊的東西，和真正購買的東西，可能非常不同。

cues.en: We're not done yet!
cues.zh: 還沒講完！

cues.en: There are just a lot of little gotchas when it comes to using recommender systems in the real world, and I don't want you to have to learn them the hard way.
cues.zh: 把推薦系統用在真實世界時，有太多細微陷阱，我不希望你也付出代價才學到。

cues.en: Another consideration is dealing with International markets.
cues.zh: 另一個考量是國際市場。

cues.en: If your recommender system spans customers in different countries, there may be specific challenges that you need to consider.
cues.zh: 如果推薦系統服務不同國家的顧客，可能有特定挑戰需要考量。

cues.en: For example, do you pool international customer data together when training a recommender system, or keep everything separated by country?
cues.zh: 例如，訓練推薦系統時，應該把各國顧客資料合併，還是依國家分開？

cues.en: In most cases, you'll want to keep things separate, since you don't want to recommend items in a foreign language to people who don't speak that language, and there may be cultural differences
cues.zh: 多數情況下，你會希望分開，因為不想向不懂某種外語的人推薦該語言的項目，而且各國的文化差異，

cues.en: that influence peoples' tastes in different countries as well.
cues.zh: 也可能影響人們的品味。

cues.en: There is also the problem of availability and content restrictions.
cues.zh: 另外還有可取得性與內容限制的問題。

cues.en: With movies in particular, movies will often be released on different schedules in different countries, and may have different licensing agreements depending on which country you're in.
cues.zh: 尤其是電影，各國上映時間往往不同，也可能依所在國家有不同的授權協議。

cues.en: You may need to filter certain movies out based on what country the user is in before presenting them as a recommendation.
cues.zh: 在呈現推薦之前，可能必須依使用者所在國家，濾除某些電影。

cues.en: Some countries have legal restrictions on what sort of content can be consumed as well, which must be taken into consideration.
cues.zh: 有些國家也對可觀看的內容有法律限制，這也必須考量。

cues.en: You can't promote content about Nazi Germany within Germany for example, nor can you promote a long list of political topics within China.
cues.zh: 例如，在德國不能推廣納粹德國相關內容，在中國也不能推廣一長串政治主題。

cues.en: Since your recommender system depends on collecting data on individual interests, there are also privacy laws to take into consideration, and these too vary by country.
cues.zh: 由於推薦系統依賴蒐集個人興趣資料，也要考量隱私法律，而各國規定也不同。

cues.en: I am not a lawyer, and these laws are changing all the time, but you'll want to consult with your company's legal department and IT security departments to ensure that any personal information you are collecting
cues.zh: 我不是律師，而且法律一直在變，但你應該諮詢公司的法務與資訊安全部門，確保蒐集的所有個人資訊，

cues.en: in the course of building your recommender system is being collected in accordance with international laws.
cues.zh: 在建立推薦系統的過程中，都依照國際法律蒐集。
